The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a1c;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8b4a1c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a1c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6248b0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056a74;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #056a74;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c00;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #705c00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a33022;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a33022;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a33022;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1f6d4b;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1f6d4b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #116785;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #116785;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #116785;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973754;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #973754;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973754;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dp, ++, dp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c00;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #705c00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #705c00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6248b0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bx, ++, bx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3b6c2b;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3b6c2b;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3b6c2b;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973754;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #973754;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973754;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hw, ++, hw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c00;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #705c00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c00;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #705c00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #705c00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6248b0;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>342d_a470</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a33022;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a33022;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a33022;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296294;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #296294;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #296294;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bh, ++, bh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3b6c2b;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3b6c2b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3b6c2b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8136a3;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8136a3;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1f6d4b;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1f6d4b;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a1c;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4a1c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a1c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3f57ab;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3f57ab;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6b62;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8d3a78;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4a1c;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8b4a1c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4a1c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #056a74;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #056a74;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6248b0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>2a28_90bf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3f57ab;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3f57ab;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3f57ab;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, aw, ++, aw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #116785;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #116785;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #116785;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8d3a78;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ef, ++, ef"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6b62;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1b6b62;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a33022;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #296294;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #296294;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #116785;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #116785;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #116785;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d3a78;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fh, ++, fh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2846_25d5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3b6c2b;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3b6c2b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3b6c2b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8d3a78;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fw, ++, fw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c00;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #705c00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #705c00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #116785;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #116785;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6b62;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b6b62;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6b62;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8d3a78;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8d3a78;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5b641c;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5b641c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5b641c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6248b0;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6248b0;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bp, ++, bp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #056a74;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #056a74;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #056a74;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8136a3;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8136a3;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>d308_4f87</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #705c00;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #705c00;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #705c00;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8136a3;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8136a3;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8136a3;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th> <th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Progeny<br/>Count</th></tr><tr> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><span style="font-size: medium;">1</span></td> <td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mp, ++, mp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
